scope: Cross-artifact design context; concise paraphrases, no reproduced publication figures

sources.title: The Science of Visual Data Communication: What Works
sources.authors: Franconeri, Padilla, Shah, Zacks and Hullman
sources.inspection: Publisher full text: abstract, scope, encoding tasks, grouping/working-memory discussion and rich/minimalistic design section; correction checked separately
sources.supported_claim: Design depends on reader tasks and knowledge; blanket decluttering has mixed evidence rather than universal performance benefits.
sources.limit: Review focuses on communication to nonspecialists, not all expert scientific workflows. Do not turn reviewed channel rankings into universal rules.
sources.visual_reference: Figures 13 and 15 provide grouping/legend and clutter contrasts; link for reading, do not reproduce.

sources.title: Corrigendum: The Science of Visual Data Communication: What Works
sources.supported_claim: Corrects color-vision/palette examples and descriptions of an uncertainty experiment.
sources.limit: Use corrected material; the correction is not a separate design efficacy study.

sources.title: Assessing Effects of Task and Data Distribution on the Effectiveness of Visual Encodings
sources.inspection: Author page and paper: abstract, introduction and experimental design
sources.supported_claim: Encoding performance varies with task and data characteristics; colored scatterplots suitable for individual comparisons can perform poorly for aggregate comparisons with many categories.
sources.limit: Tested trivariate displays and specified tasks; no universal conclusion about every academic figure or table.
sources.visual_reference: Paper Figure 1 contrasts experimental displays for read-value and compare-average tasks.

sources.title: Scientific illustration for commissioned content: Our guiding principles for conceptual figures
sources.inspection: Four-page official PDF text; pages 2 and 4 identified as published visual references
sources.supported_claim: Explain symbols and arrow meanings, organize hierarchy around the mechanism, and reconsider icon-decorated lists that would work better as tables.
sources.limit: Commissioned conceptual figures, particularly explanatory/review material; not a general quantitative chart rule or all-journal submission specification.
sources.visual_reference: Pages 2 and 4: simplified mechanism and faux-figure/table contrast.

sources.title: Preparing figures — our specifications
sources.inspection: Official graph, text, scale-bar and font sections
sources.supported_claim: This guide specifies editable standard-font text, 5–7 pt main figure text, 8 pt bold lowercase panel labels, and an avoidance preference for background gridlines.
sources.limit: Scoped Nature production instructions, not universal design optima. Recheck article/asset/stage and conflicts with supplied editor instructions. The earlier pilot's 8 pt minimum was an explicitly synthetic author/editor brief, not this specification.

sources.title: Accessibility Guide for Authors
sources.inspection: Authoring and HTML/PDF export sections; page dated 2024-08-15
sources.supported_claim: Use semantic tables and headers, non-color identifying cues and meaningful figure descriptions; verify exported accessibility metadata.
sources.limit: Venue-specific requirements can differ; visible screenshots cannot establish semantic PDF accessibility.

sources.title: Tips for Tables, Charts, and Figures
sources.inspection: Design advice, data display and concepts sections; page last updated 2024-09-03
sources.supported_claim: Match display to communication purpose, retain units/sample context, and seek prereader feedback.
sources.limit: Grant-oriented suggestions; separate mandatory application rules from general manuscript design advice.

sources.title: Layout
sources.inspection: Publisher indexed excerpt only; direct retrieval encountered identity-provider error
sources.supported_claim: The accessible excerpt describes layout as organization that clarifies communication.
sources.limit: Full column not inspected; no detailed numeric or golden-ratio prescription derived from it. Background lead only, not a required authority in the decision rules.
